title: Ang 1298–1311: Guru Arjan in Kanara
hook: no enemy, no stranger, on ang 1299
tomorrow: what does Namdev see when he looks in a mirror?

segments.voice: Yesterday, ang 1294: Kanara, the night raga, opened with a mind turning green in good company. Night, and still green. Now the fifth Guru takes up the raga.

The incoming class group chat is a crowd of strangers posting dorm photos and meal plan questions. Then someone posts a joke about Sikhs and turbans, with a laughing face. A few people react. Simran types fast, three paragraphs, thumbs shaking. Her cursor sits over send. And the page she read last night, a page into Guru Arjan's hymns in Kanara, says no one is my enemy. Does she fire back?
screen: `A CROWD OF STRANGERS.` → `A JOKE ABOUT SIKHS.` → `THREE PARAGRAPHS, THUMB ON SEND.`

segments.voice: Guru Arjan's hymns in Kanara begin on ang 1298, and on ang 1299 comes the line. In paraphrase: I've forgotten all my jealousy of others since I found the company of the holy. No one is my enemy, no one is bigaana, a stranger; I get along with everyone. Big words for a shaking-thumbs night, and Sikhs read them two ways. Both deserve a hearing. The first view: this describes a state, a mind so settled in the sangat that hostility drops away. It isn't a rule against speaking. Sikh tradition honors standing up for others, and a mind with no enemy can still say plainly: that's not okay. So answer, but without hate. The second view takes the line as a daily practice before it's a state. If no one is a stranger, the guy who posted the joke isn't either. He's someone who doesn't know you yet. So don't answer in the crowd, where everyone performs. Message him alone, or let it pass, and keep your fire. Both views agree on what the line is not. It isn't nothing matters, and it isn't permission to hate back. Here's something to tell a friend tonight: in the hymn, no stranger comes right after I forgot my jealousy. Letting go of envy comes first. Simran deletes the three paragraphs. Then she writes one line, and doesn't send it yet.
screen: `ANG 1299: NO ENEMY, NO STRANGER.` · `ONE VIEW: SPEAK UP, WITHOUT HATE.` · `THE OTHER: NOT IN THE CROWD.` · `NEITHER: NOTHING MATTERS.` · then, large: `NO STRANGER.`

segments.voice: Sit up, and notice where anger lives in you right now: the jaw, the shoulders, the hands. On each out-breath, loosen one of them a little. If someone you're angry with comes to mind, let them stay there while you keep loosening.
Ang 1298. Where Guru Arjan's hymns in Kanara begin; a page later, no one is my enemy, no one a stranger.
Your line: no stranger, not even the one who doesn't know you yet. See you tomorrow.
